title: Verifier-Guided Dynamic Task Recomposition for Multi-Agent LLM Workflows
research_question: Can a verifier-guided orchestration policy that dynamically recomposes task decomposition during execution reduce error propagation and token cost compared with fixed planner-executor multi-agent workflows on long-horizon AI tasks?
hypothesis: Multi-agent workflows fail when early decomposition mistakes propagate unchecked; inserting a lightweight verifier that selectively triggers task recomposition only at high-risk intermediate states will improve end-task success while using less compute than always-on critique or escalation policies.
motivation: The knowledge base shows recent rejected ideas clustered around uncertainty averaging and escalation policies for agent orchestration, suggesting those directions are already explored or insufficiently novel. A clearer gap is dynamic correction of decomposition itself: many agentic workflows assume the initial plan is mostly correct, yet long-horizon tasks often fail because subtask boundaries become invalid as new evidence appears. The self-adaptive systems evidence highlights the broader open problem of handling model-selection uncertainty and extending feedback-loop methods to additional domains. Translating that insight to agentic AI suggests a new direction: treat task decomposition as a revisable hypothesis and trigger recomposition only when verifier signals indicate the current decomposition no longer fits the observed execution state. This targets a core failure mode in multi-agent systems while avoiding overlap with previously rejected uncertainty-averaging and escalation proposals.
